name: Khasi

catalog_quote: In isolation words have one stress which coincides with the falling pitch on the final syllable. In context these stresses and pitch contours are deleted on all words but the final (Rabel :30).

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.deciding_source_year: 1961 (Rabel), via StressTyp2 2015 and Schiering & van der Hulst 2010
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes in both held carriers ( passage 1177; Schiering & van der Hulst 2010 pp.592 and 594, verbatim, pages verified from footers). The classification 'final, fixed-dominant, non-strict, domain word and phrase together' matches every statement seen: Rabel via StressTyp2 (final stress in isolation, deleted in context except on the last word), Khyriem 2001 via the survey (final accent in simple/complex/compound words), and held Nagaraja 1990 p.26 (stress contextual/emphatic — supports the word and phrase together caution rather than a different position); held Nagaraja 1977 phonology chapter has no stress section. Weaknesses: the chain is second-hand (database + survey quoting a 1961 grammar and an unpublished 2001 MA), Rabel p.30 is not yet obtained, and the 2014 Brill sketch by Nagaraja is unread; the survey itself flags the status of Khasi 'stress' as 'highly debatable'.
